signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: CHF/JPY is the epicentre of a massive G10 divergence as the JPY 1W avg outperformance reaches +1.283% against a -1.016% LAGGARD return for CHF, creating a 2.300% spread. While both currencies traditionally share safe-haven properties, the US-Iran war escalation has triggered a distinct JPY bid that CHF is failing to match, exacerbated by the SNB's 0.00% rate vs the BoJ's 1.0% rate creating a 100bp carry disadvantage for CHF. Market reports of a historic US-Japan yen intervention further complicate the JPY bid, though JPY COT LF net short of -124,575 suggests a massive short-covering tailwind remains. CHF is fundamentally undermined by a deeply negative ESI of -33.8, signaling persistent data misses that contrast with the JPY's neutral -0.5 print. The bilateral spread of 2.300% is nearly double the critical threshold, marking this as the dominant G10 trend. Risk: De-escalation in Middle East tensions causes a rapid mean-reversion of the safe-haven JPY bid.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Positioning + Options + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.35, testing its SMA200 at 158.05 while holding well below the SMA20/50 cluster near 161.20/43. The options market is signaling intense downside protection demand with a strong 25d RR put skew of -2.30, even as the 275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential remains intact. This options bearishness aligns with a COT speculative short of -124,575 contracts, creating a high-conviction environment for a disorderly long-liquidation if 158.00 fails. Negative USD economic surprises (ESI -15.0) and Middle East war headlines are neutralizing the carry advantage, with USD/JPY vs VIX correlation at +0.219 (z=+1.17σ) showing the pair is failing to rally on traditional risk-on triggers. A sustained break of the SMA200 would target the 155.00 handle as speculative shorts capitulate. Risk: A surprise Fed hawkish shift or US NFP beat forces a repricing of the 1.56% US real rate advantage, defending the 158.00 level.

signals.title: NZD/USD — COT vs OIS Divergence + ESI
signals.text: NZD/USD at 0.5869 sits in a bullish technical posture above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.5791-0.5829), despite a massive COT LF net short of -30,606. This spec positioning is in direct contradiction with the RBNZ's hiking stance and a stellar ESI of +76.0, the second highest in the G10. RBNZ holds at 2.5%. While the 125bp nominal carry favors the USD, the NZD real rate of -1.56% is deeply accommodative, inviting further data outperformance. Retail sentiment is also 70% short, providing a contrarian layer that supports a move toward 0.6000 as institutions and retail both find themselves on the wrong side of the data trend. Risk: A sharp reversal in commodity prices or a dovish RBNZ pivot at the Sept 2 meeting.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Volatility Premium + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD is trading at 0.7028, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6923-0.7002) ahead of next week's RBA decision. The options market is pricing an extreme 8.4% Vol Risk Premium (VRP), with IV at 14.7% vs HV30 of 6.2%, indicating that traders are paying a massive premium for protection relative to realized movement. This elevated IV environment suggests an imminent break of the current range, likely to the upside given the 73% retail short bias and the +23,616 COT net long position. The 60bp carry advantage for AUD (RBA 4.35% vs Fed 3.75%) provides a structural floor, while the mildly restrictive real rate of +0.60% supports the currency against a softening US data backdrop (USD ESI -15.0). Risk: RBA delivers a surprise dovish hold on Tuesday, prompting a vol crush and a break below the 0.7000 SMA support.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Data Strength vs Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD at 1.1525 is consolidating above its SMA20 (1.145) and SMA50 (1.1477), supported by a robust ESI of +44.1. Despite the 135bp carry disadvantage (Fed 3.75% vs ECB 2.4%), the EUR is benefiting from a trend of consistent data beats (52 beats vs 21 misses). The options market reflects this tension with a 2.7% VRP (IV 7.1% vs HV30 4.4%), signaling that the market is paying for upside protection or hedging against a breakout from the recent tight range. The 25d RR remains mildly bearish at -0.34, suggesting that while the spot price is bid, the institutional options market remains skeptical of a sustained move above the SMA200 at 1.1633. ECB holds at 2.4%. Risk: Fed's Musalem comments regarding accommodative conditions lead to a hawkish repricing of the Fed path, strengthening the USD carry floor.
